paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. The work God's people were doing was good, and opposition showed up anyway. First came a friendly offer of help, and when that got turned down, the pressure started (Ezra 4:2-4). Doing the right thing doesn't promise a quiet kitchen, and that's worth knowing before the heat hits.

Notice how the opposition changed shape. It started out sounding friendly, then turned to discouraging the people and making them afraid to build (Ezra 4:4). Then came hired counselors, an accusation, and finally a letter to the king (Ezra 4:5-6, 4:11-16). In the end, "the construction of the house of God in Jerusalem ceased" (Ezra 4:24). I think that was a heavy day for the builders, and I'm not going to joke my way around it.

But read that last verse again, because it gives a time: the work "remained at a standstill until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia" (Ezra 4:24). A standstill with an end date isn't the end of the story. If your work for the LORD has hit a stop sign, friend, keep that apron on. The story isn't over, and neither is the building.
